name: Slipcast
description:
Slipcast is defined by deliberate, aesthetically intentional cross-tier feed contamination — composers who work in this genre craft pieces designed to sound radically different depending on the quality and bandwidth of the neural feed infrastructure through which they are received. A Slipcast composition heard on a Tier 1 high-fidelity private feed sounds like one piece; the same file degraded through Tier 4 municipal infrastructure sounds like an entirely different work; experienced through an illegal Tier 6 tap on a damaged relay, it becomes something else entirely. This is not accidental — Slipcast artists spend enormous effort designing their compositions to be transformed meaningfully by infrastructure decay.

The genre emerged from composers who were frustrated by the assumption that lower-tier listeners were receiving an inferior version of upper-tier art. Slipcast inverts this entirely: lower-tier degradation is a compositional element, not a failure. Some Slipcast theorists argue that only listeners in Tiers 4-6 experience the 'intended' version of a Slipcast work, since the compositions are built around the specific harmonic artifacts produced by municipal-grade feed compression. This position is deeply controversial but has gained significant critical traction.
creator: various
tier_availability: All tiers; experienced differently by each tier
legality: Legal; some compositions investigated for intentional feed manipulation
audience: All tiers; critically acclaimed across socioeconomic spectrum; particularly embraced in Tier 3-5
cultural_impact: Slipcast has generated more critical theory per released composition than almost any other genre in GLMZ's contemporary scene, partly because it forces listeners and critics to confront the politics of infrastructure as aesthetics. It has been adopted as a cause by feed equity activists, who use Slipcast's existence as evidence that the tiered neural feed system is not a neutral technical distinction but a cultural stratification mechanism. Several Tier 1 music institutions have attempted to commission Slipcast works, a development that purists consider a fundamental misunderstanding of the genre's premise.
story_hooks: A Slipcast composer discovers that a specific degraded version of her work, heard only through a single failing relay station, has developed a small fanatical following who believe it contains subliminal messaging she never intentionally encoded

A Tier 1 infrastructure upgrade threatens to destroy the specific feed-decay characteristics that a beloved Slipcast composition was built around — its composer must decide whether to fight the upgrade or let the work die
Someone is deliberately sabotaging feed relays in precise patterns, and an investigator realizes the sabotage is creating a specific unauthorized Slipcast composition that can only be heard city-wide
